 Among the Best: three Jesuit seniors named National Merit semifinalists
 Callum Macdonald ’29 and Joseph Alfieri ’29 
 • 
 November 4, 2026 
 Jack Stouder ’28 
 Every year, over a million high school seniors across the nation compete in the National Merit Scholarship competition. However, only 16,000 are selected as semifinalists, and this year, three of Jesuit High School Sacramento’s seniors have qualified: Drew Eandi ’27, Ian Kim ’27, and Jack McWilliams ’27. 
 This competition for college scholarships is based on Preliminary SAT/National Merit Scholarship Qualifying Test (PSAT/NMSQT) scores. Semifinalists are recognized for scoring in the top one percent in the United States.  
 While certainly impressive on college applications, this competition can also help make college more affordable and available. 
 “Some colleges also offer their own merit scholarships just for becoming a semifinalist, which is a really great way to save on tuition,” said Jack. 
 Success on the test is not a result of excessive studying or extensive memorization; instead, it comes down to a student’s understanding of a topic.  
 “There’s really no better test prep than understanding the material,” Jack said. “The people who succeed are the ones who understand the underlying concepts behind these core subjects. Jesuit really sets you up to do that.” 
 Additionally, the ability to think critically is imperative. Students can develop this skill by challenging themselves and persevering through adversity. 
 “Jesuit definitely encourages that kind of curiosity, which keeps me motivated to put a lot of effort into these subjects,” Jack said. “Struggling on a problem and still pushing through is what makes me a better thinker.” 
 Drew Eandi also believes that a Jesuit education was crucial to his success.  
 “I remember favoring Jesuit for how much the teachers cared,” said Drew. “When teachers were involved, they were conducting their classes and discussions, all approachably responsive to questions.” 
 As they prepare their applications to become finalists in the National Merit Scholarship competition, these standout students will continue to be challenged to grow and succeed at Jesuit.
